title: Fix the shared parts tray
prompt:
Byte wrote `add_part`, which puts a part on a tray and returns the tray. Each call without a tray should start a fresh, empty tray. Instead, every call piles onto the same tray.

Run `python3 tray.py` to see the bug, then fix the function so the program prints `['gear']`, then `['fuse']`.
hints: The default `tray=[]` is made once, when Python reads the `def` line, and then every call shares it.
Use `None` as the default instead, and make the new list inside the function.
`def add_part(part, tray=None):` then `if tray is None:` and `tray = []` as the first lines of the body.
explain_after: A default value is evaluated only once, so a list default is shared between calls [py-086]. The fix is the one the Python tutorial gives: default to `None` and make the list inside the function [py-087].
